learn.hook: Numbers have personalities! Some are even, some are odd, some are 'supercells' that tower over their neighbours.
points: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
Even + even = even, odd + odd = even, and even + odd = odd.
The digit sum of a number is what you get when you add its digits: for 347 it is 3 + 4 + 7 = 14.
In a row of numbers, a supercell is a number bigger than all its neighbours. A number at either end has only one neighbour.
Collatz game: if a number is even, halve it; if it is odd, multiply by 3 and add 1. Every number anyone has tried so far ends at 1.

example.q: Play the Collatz game starting with 6.

learn.reallife: Pairing up children for a game works only when the number is even; shopkeepers quickly check bills using digit sums.

games.title: Will the answer be even or odd?

items.text: The smallest 3-digit number with digit sum 5 is ___
Odd + odd always gives an ___ number.
In the row 4, 9, 2, 7, 3 the supercells are 9 and ___

quiz.q: Is the sum 37 + 48 + 15 even or odd?
quiz.explain: Odd + even + odd: the two odd numbers make an even, and even + even is even. The total is 100.
quiz.mistake: Thinks that adding any odd number makes the answer odd

quiz.q: What is the digit sum of 9078?
quiz.mistake: Skips a digit or makes an adding slip

quiz.q: How many supercells are in this row: 5, 8, 3, 6, 1, 4? (A supercell is bigger than all its neighbours.)
quiz.explain: 8 is bigger than 5 and 3; 6 is bigger than 3 and 1; 4 at the end has only one neighbour, 1, and is bigger. So there are 3.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a number at the end has only one neighbour

quiz.q: Start the Collatz game at 5 (even → halve, odd → × 3 + 1). What is the third number after 5?
quiz.explain: 5 → 16 → 8 → 4. The third number after 5 is 4.
quiz.mistake: Counts 5 itself as a step, or stops too early

quiz.q: Arjun adds five odd numbers. The answer must be...
quiz.explain: Four odd numbers make two even pairs, and the fifth odd number makes the total odd. For example 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding odd numbers always gives an even answer

quiz.q: Which of these numbers has digits that add up to 10?
quiz.mistake: Adds only the first two digits

quiz.q: Meena says: 'Adding two even numbers always gives an even number.' Is she right?
quiz.explain: Each even number is made of pairs. Putting pairs together still gives only pairs, so the sum is even.
quiz.mistake: Thinks large even numbers might behave differently

quiz.q: Kabir looks at the numbers from 1 to 20. How many of them have a digit sum of 5?
quiz.explain: Only 5 and 14 (1 + 4 = 5) have a digit sum of 5 between 1 and 20.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the single-digit number 5, or includes 23 which is bigger than 20

teach.ask: Gappu has 7 + 9 written in the sand: 'Without adding, can you tell if the answer is even or odd? How?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Odd + odd makes even because the two leftover ones pair up. Clever!
teach.nudge: Why does odd + odd turn out even? What happens to the leftovers?

learn.hook: MALAYALAM reads the same backwards! Numbers can play this mirror game too.
points: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards: 121, 4334, 7 and the word MALAYALAM.
Every 1-digit number is a palindrome. A 3-digit palindrome has the same first and last digit, like 505.
Reverse-and-add: add a number to its reverse, then repeat with the answer until you get a palindrome.
Clocks show palindrome times too, like 12:21 and 10:01.

example.q: Do reverse-and-add on 57 until you get a palindrome.

learn.reallife: Look for palindrome bus numbers, car number plates and dates like 22-02-2022!

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is a palindrome?
quiz.explain: 2442 backwards is 2442. The others change when reversed, for example 2424 becomes 4242.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number with repeating digits is always a palindrome

quiz.q: How many 2-digit palindromes are there?
quiz.explain: They are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99, which makes 9. (00 is not a 2-digit number.)
steps: Both digits must be the same
quiz.mistake: Counts 00 as a 2-digit number

quiz.q: Do reverse-and-add on 48: 48 + 84 = 132. Then 132 + 231 = ?
quiz.explain: 132 + 231 = 363, which is a palindrome.
quiz.mistake: Doubles 132 instead of adding its reverse (264)

quiz.q: Riya's digital clock shows 10:01. Is it a palindrome time?
options: Yes, 1001 reads the same both ways
quiz.explain: Ignoring the colon, the digits 1-0-0-1 read the same forwards and backwards.
quiz.mistake: Compares the two halves without reversing the second one

quiz.q: What is the smallest 3-digit palindrome?
quiz.explain: The first digit must be 1 and the last digit must match it, so the smallest is 1_1 with 0 in the middle: 101.
quiz.mistake: Chooses 100, which reads 001 backwards

quiz.q: Which of these state languages is spelled as a palindrome in English capital letters?
quiz.explain: MALAYALAM backwards is M-A-L-A-Y-A-L-A-M, exactly the same.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the first and last letters

quiz.q: How many 3-digit palindromes start with the digit 5?
quiz.explain: They look like 5_5, and the middle digit can be any of 0 to 9: 505, 515, ..., 595. That is 10.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the middle digit can be 0

quiz.q: Reverse-and-add on 23 gives a palindrome after how many steps?
quiz.explain: 23 + 32 = 55, which is already a palindrome. So it takes just 1 step.
quiz.mistake: Keeps adding after a palindrome has already appeared

teach.ask: Gappu writes 1221 in the sand: 'Someone called this a palindrome. What does that mean?'
teach.praise: Chirp! It reads the same forwards and backwards, like MALAYALAM. I'll spot them on number plates!
teach.nudge: What happens when you read it from the other end?

learn.hook: Pick almost any 4-digit number, follow a simple recipe, and you will always land on 6174. Spooky? No, it's maths!
points: Take a 4-digit number whose digits are not all the same.
Arrange its digits from largest to smallest, and again from smallest to largest.
Subtract the smaller number from the larger one. Keep zeros: 0378 counts as a 4-digit arrangement.
Repeat with the answer. You always reach 6174 within 7 steps, and 7641 − 1467 = 6174 brings it back to itself.
This was discovered by D. R. Kaprekar, a maths teacher from Maharashtra. For 3-digit numbers the routine ends at 495.
learn.reallife: It's a great party trick: ask a friend for a 4-digit number and tell them where they'll end up before they start!

games.title: Kaprekar's recipe
games.prompt: Put the steps in the right order
items: Pick a 4-digit number whose digits are not all the same
Arrange its digits to make the largest and the smallest numbers
Subtract the smaller number from the larger
Repeat with the answer until you reach 6174

quiz.q: What is Kaprekar's constant for 4-digit numbers?
quiz.explain: Every 4-digit number (digits not all the same) reaches 6174, and 7641 − 1467 = 6174 again.
quiz.mistake: Picks one of the arranged numbers, or the 3-digit constant 495

quiz.q: Start with 2005. Arrange its digits largest-first and smallest-first, then subtract. What do you get?
quiz.explain: Largest: 5200. Smallest: 0025, which is 25. 5200 − 25 = 5175.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the original number (3195), keeps only one zero in front (4995) or adds (5225)

quiz.q: Joseph uses 6174 in Kaprekar's routine. What does he get next?
quiz.explain: Largest 7641 − smallest 1467 = 6174. It comes back to itself, so the routine stops there.
quiz.mistake: Stops after arranging the digits instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Why can't we use 3333 in Kaprekar's routine?
options: All its digits are the same, so the answer is 0 at once
quiz.explain: 3333 − 3333 = 0, so the routine gets stuck. Other palindromes like 4224 work fine.
quiz.mistake: Thinks palindromes cannot be used

quiz.q: For 3-digit numbers (digits not all the same), Kaprekar's routine ends at which number?
quiz.explain: For 3 digits the routine ends at 495, because 954 − 459 = 495.
quiz.mistake: Uses the 4-digit constant or reverses the digits (594)

quiz.q: Aisha starts with 4321. What is the first subtraction answer?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to borrow (3097 or 3187), or adds instead (5555)

quiz.q: Next step from 3087: the arrangements are 8730 and 0378. What is 8730 − 378?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing slip, or adds instead of subtracting (9108)

quiz.q: Who discovered the special property of 6174?
options: D. R. Kaprekar, a maths teacher from Maharashtra
quiz.explain: D. R. Kaprekar found this routine, which is why 6174 is called Kaprekar's constant.
quiz.mistake: Guesses another famous Indian mathematician

teach.ask: Gappu has the number 2196: 'Show me the Kaprekar trick! What do I do?'
teach.praise: Wow! Biggest minus smallest, again and again, and I reached 6174. Magic maths!
teach.nudge: After arranging the digits two ways, what do I do with those two numbers?
